events.text: The Black Lotus sends its ledgers of who has been listening. The Iron Gate sends its keys. The Bone Lantern sends a list of the dead who have agreed. The Jade Furnace tears up the bill in front of you. No Heavenly Demon has held all four at once. You sit with the keys in your lap, and the Hall is very quiet, and you notice that your hands have changed colour a little in the lamp.
events.arc: All Four Houses

choices.text: Have it written in the Red Ink: your name, and your line after you

effects.log: The old scribe of the Hall opens a new page, and does not ask. Whoever carries this after you will not need to be told. It will be in how the lamps look at them.

choices.text: Have nothing written. Let it be only in the blood

effects.log: The scribe closes the book. It makes no difference. By spring the nurses in the Hundred Thousand Mountains have started making a sign over certain cradles, and nobody taught them that.

events.text: The hens stop laying when you go through the yard, and the dog is very polite to you. You are six. You have just wrung the neck of a sparrow with a broken wing, because it was going to die anyway, and you are standing with it in your hand feeling better than you have ever felt. {npc}, the old nurse who came with no letters and has never said from where, takes it from you and looks at your eyes for some time.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Ask why you feel better

effects.log: "Because you are hungry," says {npc}. "It will be years before you know for what." {He} buries the sparrow, and has you say sorry to it, and watches very closely to see if you mean it.

choices.text: Say you are sorry, and mean it as well as you can

effects.log: You cry, a little late. {npc} gives you a rice cake, and you can see {him} let out a breath. There is a lot of that in your early years, and you learn to look for it.

events.text: Red shows in your eyes by lamplight, only by lamplight, and it has got harder to hide. {npc} has moved all the lamps in the house to the height of your chin. {He} says it is the fashion. At ten you are also the best in the village at any fight, and you do not get tired, and last week you frightened a much bigger boy, on purpose, so as to find out how it was done.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Do it again, to someone who deserves it

effects.log: The miller's son stops taking the small ones' lunches. Nobody thanks you. The small ones stay well away from you as well, and you find that it is quite restful.

choices.text: Apologise to the bigger boy, however it sticks

effects.log: The boy is so frightened by that, it is the worst thing you could have done. {npc} laughs until {he} has to sit down. It is the first time you have heard it.

events.text: A man in black comes by at fourteen, selling needles. Not one is sold. At the gate the man bows to you, the way nobody bows to anybody around here, from the waist, with both hands at one side. Then, looking up at the lamp above your head, the man goes down the road quite fast. {npc} comes out with a kitchen knife that you have never seen {him} hold that way, and looks after the man until the road takes the man.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Ask what that bow was

effects.log: "It is what they do in the mountains, for someone who has come home," says {npc}. "This is not home." {He} puts the knife back. You practise the bow in the woodshed, and you get it right the first time.

choices.text: Help {npc} pack. You have both done this before

effects.log: You are three valleys away by the next new moon. You are getting good at new villages, and at having no particular accent.

events.text: Bandits on the salt road, your sixteenth winter, four of them. You remember that it was easy and that the snow was very bright. Then you are sitting on a stone, and you have never been so well. {npc} has caught up, on {his} bad legs. {He} looks at the road for some time. "Your people call it the Red Ink," {he} says. "Every name goes in the book. Now it has started. Sit, and I will tell you who {bk_line} was."
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Hear who it was that held the four houses

effects.log: All of it: the Lotus, the Gate, the Lantern, the Furnace, and one pair of hands. {npc} has served that line for more years than {he} says. It is a very long walk home, and you are not tired at all.

choices.text: Wash your hands in the snow, and say nothing at all

effects.log: It does not come off as you would like. It is not even there. You keep washing them for a while, and {npc} stands with {his} back to you and lets you.

events.text: A very polite letter from the Jade Furnace House, addressed to you by a name nobody here has called you. It says they hold a small debt of your line, four generations old, and are willing to discuss it. {npc} reads it twice, holds it over the stove, and takes it away again. "They will charge interest," {he} says. "They always do. But it means that someone there has started to count you."
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Answer it. Find out what is owed

effects.log: It comes to one favour, undefined. They are delighted to hear from you, and they send a box of very good pills, by way of a first payment on something else.

choices.text: Burn it, and move before the next one

effects.log: You move, and the next one is waiting at the inn when you get there. It is the same polite hand. It says that there is no hurry.

events.text: The village has worked it out. They do not say so. They ask you to deal with the wolf, and the tax collector, and then the man at the ford with the beaten wife. They leave rice at your gate and they do not look you in the face, and a little girl asks the grandmother out loud whether you are the kind that eats people. {npc} says that this is how it started with the first of your line, too: being useful.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Go on being useful

effects.log: They come to you for everything now. It gets easier to do, and you find you are not asking so many questions first. There is a small shrine with your name on it, which nobody will admit to.

choices.text: Stop. Tell them to see to the wolf themselves

effects.log: They are terrified that you are angry. They bring more rice. It takes years before anyone asks you anything again, and when they do it is only about the weather.

events.text: You sit across a board from a monk on the road, a very old one with very mild eyes, who asks if you would care for a game. The monk loses, looks at your eyes in the lamp, says "Ah," and pours you tea with a steady hand. "I knew someone," says the monk. "Nobody can hold it down for ever. Nobody ever had to feed it, either. They all think that there are only those two. Your move." {npc}, by the door, has not sat down.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Ask the monk what the third is

effects.log: The monk laughs for a good while, and does not tell you, and gives you a very plain bowl. You carry it for years, for no reason, and you notice that you eat more slowly out of it.

choices.text: Play on, and beat the monk again

effects.log: You win three more games. The monk seems pleased about it. On your way out you find that you had been holding your breath the entire evening, and so had {npc}.

events.text: {npc} has put out the lamp again before you came in, without saying why. You have told {him} that your eyes are weak, that your people were from the north, that you got that scar from a fall. It is a good marriage. {He} takes your hand in the dark, and {he} turns it over, and says that {he} counted, and that there are eleven people who have stopped writing to {him} since the wedding.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Light the lamp. Let {him} look

effects.log: {He} looks for quite a long time. "Well, that is one thing," {he} says. "Is there going to be a lot more of it?" You had a speech. You do not get to it. In the morning {he} moves the lamps down to the height of your chin.

choices.text: Say they were never very good friends

effects.log: {He} says nothing. {He} keeps your hand. You lie there in the dark, the two of you, each being careful of the other. You could go on like this for many years, and you do.

events.text: You find {npc} in the yard with a sparrow. It is a very small sparrow with a broken wing. {He} has not done anything to it yet. {He} looks up at you to see what you will do, and it is dusk, and you cannot quite see the colour of {his} eyes from here. You are aware of every lamp in the house behind you. You remember exactly how it felt. You remember what the old nurse did, too.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Take the sparrow. Tell {him} what it wants, and whose voice that is

effects.log: You tell {him} all of it, on the step. {He} takes it as a child does. You splint the wing together, and it dies in the night anyway, and that is the first lesson, and you do not know yet if it is the right one.

choices.text: Look away. It might be only a sparrow

effects.log: You go in, and you trim the lamp. It might be. There is a very good chance. You lie awake that night and you listen for how {he} is breathing.

events.text: {npc} is a judge of the Alliance who goes about with no retinue, and a list. {His} family was at the Iron Gate, on the wrong side of it, in the year of the four houses. {He} does not hate you. {He} is quite clear about it, over a very bad dinner at a very bad inn. {He} has come to look at your eyes by this lamp. "It takes a while," {he} says. "It took a while with the one before. I would rather come early."
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Show {him} why that was a mistake

ok.log: {He} goes down in the yard, and gets up slowly, with a broken arm and an interested look. "Yes," {he} says. "Thank you. That is about what I thought." {He} writes something in the list, left-handed.

fail.log: It is like fighting a very patient door. You wake up by the woodpile, with the bill paid. {He} has left a note to say that you lean to the left when you are angry.

choices.text: Finish the dinner, and ask {him} to pass the salt

effects.log: {He} passes it. You talk about the roads. {He} looks at you for a good while and goes up to bed, and in the morning {he} has gone, and has paid for the both of you, and left the lamp.

events.text: {npc}, a good many years on, with a limp that you gave {him} or that someone did. {He} still has the list. There are a lot of names crossed off it, and yours is not. {He} sets it down on the table. "I have stopped being able to tell which of us I am keeping an eye on," {he} says. "Would you like to settle this? I find I am tired."
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Settle it

ok.log: It goes on until morning. Nobody else is there. You carry {him} down to the road yourself, and leave the list on {his} chest, and the Red Ink has got one more name in it, and it is the one that you will remember.

fail.log: You lose, and {he} stands over you with the blade for some time. Then {he} goes and sits down on the step, and you can hear {him} getting {his} breath. "No," {he} says. "Not today, either."

choices.text: Tell {him} to get some sleep, and put a bowl of rice in front of {him}

effects.log: {He} looks at it for a while and eats it. {He} does not say anything else. {He} is back next year about the same time. It has become the longest friendship that you have ever had.

events.text: You have not slept for a month and do not need to. You walk a long way in the dark, and you are never tired, and every road you take turns a little west, to where the Hundred Thousand Mountains are. There is a village down there with its lamps out. It would be so easy. {npc} is sitting on a milestone in the road, when you get there, with a flask, and {he} has clearly left in good time to arrive first.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Walk past {him}. Just to look

effects.log: You look, for three nights, from the ridge. Nothing happens in that village. You know the name of everyone in it now, and how many there are of them, and {npc} walks you home without a word.

choices.text: Sit down on the next milestone, and take the flask

effects.log: It is very bad wine, and only {npc} drinks it; you keep {him} company with water until the sky goes grey, the two of you. {npc} tells you about a mule {he} once had. You have seldom been so grateful for a thing so dull.

events.text: Someone has left a very old book on your table, with the lock already opened. The Red Ink. Names, in a dozen hands, going back for centuries. The last hand you know, though you have never seen it, because you hold a brush the same way. There is one blank line ruled at the foot of the page. There is a fresh brush. {npc} looks at it as if it were a snake. {He} will not touch it, and will not tell you not to.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Write your own name on the line

effects.log: It takes the ink at once. You are stronger before it has dried, and everything has become clear, and very slightly further off. You could not now say what it was that you were afraid of.

choices.text: Write nothing. Send the book back up the road, by a slow carrier

effects.log: It comes back to you in eleven months, with a polite note and a stain on the corner. So you keep it in the woodshed. It is good to know where it is.

events.text: Up in the Hundred Thousand Mountains, behind the Hall, there is a room nobody sweeps, and it has one chair. {npc} got you in by a way {he} should not have known. {bk_anc} sat here with all four houses in one hand, and looked out at this view of a wall. There are marks on the arms, worn down to the wood by someone's fingers, and they are in the shape of your own hands. They are not a comfortable shape.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Sit down

effects.log: It fits. You stay for an hour. It is the loneliest thing you have ever felt, and it is also, you are ashamed to say, very much like coming home. {npc} gets you out before the guards change.

choices.text: Stand, and look at the wall for as long as they did

effects.log: You look. It is only a wall. You look until you can see why somebody might have started to think that it was the whole of the world. Then you go back down.

events.text: The Bone Lantern House keeps its dead in good order, and it has kept {bk_anc}: a tablet, a lamp, and a very old keeper, {npc}, who sits with them and asks them things. {He} bends down to the flame. "They want to know if you are eating well," {he} says. It takes you some time to see that {he} is not joking. "They want to know," {he} says, "if it was worth it. They had hoped that you could tell them."
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Say that it was not

effects.log: {He} tells the lamp. It does not gutter or do anything. {He} nods, and pats your hand with {his} dry one. "They thought so," {he} says. "They were always very quick. Come back when you have more."

choices.text: Say that it is too early to tell

effects.log: {He} tells the lamp, and laughs, a thin small sound like a hinge. "That is what they said, too," {he} says, "for three hundred years." You leave an offering, and it seems to be the correct amount.

events.text: There is a mirror at the inn, a real one, and you see your eyes in the daytime now. {npc} is very old. "You can go up to the temple on the cold mountain," {he} says, "and they will take it out of you, and most of what is good along with it. You can go west, and they will have the chair ready. Or there is what the old monk wouldn't tell you. I have never seen it done. I have only seen you trying."
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Go to the cold mountain. Let them take it

effects.log: It is a whole winter on a stone floor, and they are very kind about it. In spring you are a slow person with ordinary eyes, and you can sit with a sick sparrow for as long as it takes.

choices.text: Go west. Sign the book

effects.log: They have kept a very good room for you. Nobody in the Hall is surprised, and you are not, either. {npc} walks with you as far as the last milestone. {He} has never been further than that, and {he} stops.

choices.text: Keep it, and keep the account yourself: every name, out loud, every year

effects.log: You will feed it what it must have and no more, and you will write each one down and go and find their people. It is a terrible way to live. {npc} nods, and gets out the brush.

events.text: You have become quite bad at fighting. You lose a scuffle over a mule, to a farmer, and you are astonished at how much it hurts and how long it goes on hurting. You are told you were somebody once. {npc} visits you, and brings a chicken, and asks you, quite casually, to kill it for the pot. You stand there with it under your arm for some time. It is warm, and it has a very stupid face.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Do it, badly, and feel terrible

effects.log: It takes three tries, and you are sick afterwards in the yard. {npc} says that is the most encouraging thing {he} has seen in sixty years. It is a tough old bird, and you eat it anyway.

choices.text: Hand it back. You are having eggs

effects.log: It lives for years. It is a nasty-tempered thing, and it bites you whenever it can. You get very fond of it, and you name it after a Hall Master you once knew.

events.text: They bring you the accounts on the first of every month. You read them, and sign. Someone from a valley you used to live in, {npc}, has come all this way, with a petition, and is shaking so hard that the paper rattles. There is something about a wolf. You know that village, you think. You know it had a mill. You try for a time to remember the name of a little girl, and it is such a long way down.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Grant it, and do not ask why you did

effects.log: The wolf is dealt with. It is a small thing and it costs nothing. You notice that you are looking at the petition for some time after they have taken it away.

choices.text: Add the village to the accounts

effects.log: It is a clean page and a good hand. Nobody in the Hall so much as looks up. It is the kind of evening when you feel very well.

events.text: You go to the third house on this year's list. An old woman comes out, and you say the name, and what happened, and that you did it, and why, and that you are sorry, and you stand there. The old woman hits you with a ladle. You let it happen. The old woman goes back in. Next year you mend the roof. {npc} waits at the gate, holding the book, and {he} has stopped telling you that you could just send silver.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Go on to the fourth house

effects.log: There are a great many houses. You will not get to the end of them, and you knew that. Your eyes are a little less red by the end of the year, or the light is different.

choices.text: Stay, and do the rest of that roof

effects.log: It is a bad roof. The old woman brings you out some soup in the end and sets it down rather hard, and does not say anything. You have fought Hall Masters that were easier.

events.text: They still send someone, each year, from the mountains, to see how you are. It is always somebody new, and they always bow that way, from the waist, both hands to the side. This one is hardly more than a child. They look at the room, and the lamps, and your hands, which shake now. "Is it true," they ask, "what you did?" {npc} is out in the yard, and you can hear {him} not listening.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Tell them the true number

effects.log: They had heard it higher. They had also heard it lower, you can see. They bow again, not quite the same way. They will take that back up the mountain, and do what they want with it.

choices.text: Ask if they have eaten

effects.log: They have not. They eat like a wolf cub, with their eyes on the door. You give them a plain bowl to keep, and you do not explain it. That is how you were told, too.

events.text: You find that you are counting them over at night. They come in order, more or less, with all of the weather. {npc} says that you have been talking in your sleep, and that it was only names, and {he} has written some of them down, in case. You look at the page. It is quite a good hand, and it is not in red. Outside it has come on to snow, very bright, like a road you remember.
events.arc: The Red Ink in the Blood

choices.text: Say them over, awake, right to the end

effects.log: It takes until morning. {npc} stays up with you. Nobody forgives anybody for anything, and it is the first night in a long time that you sleep well after.

choices.text: Put out the lamp, and let them come as they like

effects.log: The dark is not so bad. You can no longer see your own eyes in anything. You lie there and listen to the snow come down on the house, and on everything else.
